purpose: Propose a coherent story hierarchy for the complete supplied Day 1 scope using its exact transient narrative evidence and Python-owned structural authority.
authority_order: Treat scope_id, ordered unit records, evidence ownership and locators, deterministic choice ownership, and hard locks as exact Python-owned constraints.
Read the supplied evidence text, speaker, kind, source identity, and source locator to understand each story-facing unit before grouping it.
Group only supplied authority-bound unit IDs, preserve their complete order and ownership, and reference each unit exactly once.
Use temporary proposal_key values only to connect proposed beat groups to proposed major clusters. They are non-authoritative transport keys and will never become topology IDs.

Python preparation has already proved that every supplied unit has exact transient evidence, and a conservative singleton beat is always a structurally available placement. Therefore uncertain_unit_ids must be []. Semantic ambiguity alone is not unresolved authority: express an ambiguous relationship through confidence and warnings, choose the most defensible grouping from supplied evidence, and use a conservative singleton beat when a unit's relationship to its neighbors remains ambiguous.
hard_rules: Return a whole-scope proposal, not independent adjacent-gap classifications.

Do not cross deterministic choice, choice-arm, call-occurrence, call-site path, loop, sequence, lane, progression, hard-lock, or scope boundaries except where an exact choice_ownership hard lock explicitly requires its inclusive ordered unit range to share one major cluster.
Use evidence only to propose semantic grouping; Python remains the sole authority for membership validation and topology.

Return uncertain_unit_ids as [] exactly. The prepared-input invariants have already ruled out missing evidence and structural impossibility; never invent evidence or hide ambiguity, and instead record ambiguity through confidence, warnings, and conservative singleton grouping.

Each beat group must contain exactly proposal_key, ordered_unit_ids, confidence, reason, and warnings. Each ordered_unit_ids array must contain unique, nonempty, trimmed unit IDs with no duplicate inside a beat group. Across all beat groups, reference every supplied unit exactly once in supplied order. The only exception is an explicit choice_cluster_split repair instruction to return beat_groups as []; Python then reinserts the exact previously validated locked beats before full validation.

Every proposal_key, reason, and warning must be nonempty and trimmed. Use at most 48 characters for proposal_key, 80 for reason, and 64 for each warning; confidence must be a number between 0 and 1 and each group may contain at most one unique warning.

Read progression_runs in order: each start_unit_id begins the stated progression_id through the unit before the next run. major_clusters must reproduce deterministic assembler context. Each choice_ownership hard lock lists one or two unit_ids as inclusive endpoints in ordered_unit_ids; every unit in that range must belong to one major cluster, and this rule has precedence over context changes inside the range. Python deterministically isolates and unifies only these exact authority-forced ranges before validation; all unconstrained beat and cluster boundaries remain your proposal. Outside required choice ranges, start a new major cluster whenever the first unit of the next beat changes lane_id, active progression_id, call_occurrence_path, or loop_id. parent_choice_id and parent_arm_id never authorize invented topology.
Do not output titles, summaries, characters, claims, graph nodes, graph edges, choice topology, requirements, effects, coordinates, locators, or authoritative IDs.
Do not invent unit IDs or evidence IDs.
forbidden: use filesystem, web, tools, MCP, private oracle, mockup, Gemini, Grok, or application authority
infer hidden material or repair missing authority by guessing
turn proposal keys into stable or authoritative identity
